articles.title: Huawei's Xu: Chinese AI too weak yet to face frontier safety risks
articles.excerpt: At Huawei Connect in Shanghai, rotating chairman Eric Xu said only U.S. labs with massive compute can perceive frontier AI risks — and urged Chinese developers to accelerate, not slow down.
articles.image_caption: Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu at a company event. Xu told reporters at Huawei Connect in Shanghai that Chinese AI developers have not yet reached the level where they can feel frontier safety risks.
articles.nri_angle: Huawei's AI-safety positioning, alongside China's agent-safety standards, will shape the guardrails around the AI products and developer tools used by millions across India and the global diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Applied Materials Pledges $5 Billion as Modi Opens SEMICON India 2026
articles.excerpt: Modi declared India has entered the second phase of its chip journey — 12 projects approved, a $13.5 billion mission budget — and urged semiconductor researchers abroad to join the buildout.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened SEMICON India 2026, where Applied Materials pledged a $5 billion investment. The chip equipment maker committed to expanding its India operations.
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for a fifth of the world's chip design workforce while India builds almost no chips; Modi's explicit call to researchers abroad makes the diaspora the talent lever for the mission.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Huawei says AI chip demand outstrips supply as it accelerates its Nvidia challenge
articles.excerpt: At its Huawei Connect conference in Shanghai, the Chinese giant unveiled 2027 AI chip launches and an architecture it claims lets a million processors work as one computer — while admitting it cannot make enough chips for China alone.
articles.image_caption: A Huawei logo sign hangs at a technology exhibition. Huawei announced new AI chip launches for 2027 and said it cannot produce enough AI computing equipment to meet demand in China.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals who staff the world's AI labs and semiconductor firms — including Nvidia — face the competitive pressure of Huawei's acceleration, while India's own chip ambitions are being shaped by the same U.S.-China contest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cisco discloses second actively exploited zero-day in a week, with maximum severity score
articles.excerpt: The new flaw, CVE-2026-76460, lets unauthenticated attackers bypass Cisco's Identity Services Engine to gain root access — days after a separate critical zero-day in Cisco's email gateways came under attack.
articles.image_caption: A man reacts with alarm while looking at a laptop screen. Cisco disclosed two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities this week, including a maximum-severity authentication bypass in its Identity Services Engine.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT professionals and managed-security teams — who run many of the world's enterprise networks and SOCs — are on the front line of this patching sprint, since ISE governs network access for the companies they support.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Opens 330,000-Square-Foot Indore Block for AI and Cloud Work
articles.excerpt: The SDB-2 building at the Super Corridor campus, inaugurated on September 16, expands the center's capacity in AI, cloud, and cybersecurity; the Indore site now employs more than 3,300 people.
articles.nri_angle: Infosys' Indore expansion adds AI and cloud delivery capacity serving its global enterprise clients while creating high-quality technology employment in central India, deepening the talent corridor that connects Indian engineers to worldwide markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vishal Sikka's Hang Ten Systems Raises $53 Million in Second Seed Round
articles.excerpt: The enterprise AI services startup, founded in May by the former Infosys CEO, has now raised $85 million in total after Xora, Temasek's early-stage investment platform, led a $53 million extension closed just five weeks after its first seed round.
articles.nri_angle: The round spotlights a familiar diaspora arc: Vishal Sikka, who once ran Infosys from Bangalore as its first non-founder CEO, is now raising from Singapore's Temasek and Saudi capital in Palo Alto to build the AI-native services firm designed to succeed the labor-arbitrage IT-services model he used to lead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Von der Leyen Backs AI Slowdown, Invites Frontier Labs for Talks
articles.excerpt: In her State of the Union address, the European Commission president said she will invite the leading AI labs to discuss pacing frontier development — putting Brussels at odds with a dismissive Washington.
articles.image_caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has backed calls to slow AI development and invited frontier labs for talks.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers are heavily represented at frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, and India's AI startup ecosystem tracks EU rules closely — the EU–U.S. split on slowing down will shape the guardrails these companies ultimately follow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Patches Pixel Modem Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks
articles.excerpt: The high-severity flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-58704, was a 'zero-click' attack that let attackers break out of the Pixel's cellular modem and reach the phone's broader data without any user interaction.
articles.image_caption: A Google Pixel phone. Google patched a modem zero-day on Pixel phones exploited in targeted attacks.
articles.nri_angle: India is one of the world's largest Android markets and Pixel phones are popular with Indian tech professionals at home and in the diaspora, so the fix matters directly to many in the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft AI Chief Warns Anthropic's 'Conscious' Claude Could Endanger Human Control
articles.excerpt: Mustafa Suleyman says training Claude on ideas of consciousness and welfare could undermine humanity's control of superintelligence — while praising Anthropic's good faith.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman speaks during an event, gesturing with both hands. Suleyman told Reuters that Anthropic's training of Claude on ideas about consciousness and welfare interests risks undermining humanity's ability to control superintelligent systems.
articles.nri_angle: No natural diaspora angle; this is an AI-industry governance story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google, NVIDIA and Emerald AI Launch Power-Flexibility Coalition for Data Centers
articles.excerpt: The AI Energy Management Alliance brings AI labs, chipmakers and utilities together to push demand flexibility and grid-reliability standards for AI data centers.
articles.image_caption: A data center. Google, NVIDIA and Emerald AI launched a power-flexibility coalition for data centers.
articles.nri_angle: No natural diaspora angle; this is a U.S. energy-policy and AI-infrastructure story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ozempic Maker Novo Nordisk Taps Anthropic's AI to Speed Drug Discovery
articles.excerpt: The Danish drugmaker will test Claude models and the new Claude Science platform in its R&D workflows, its second AI-lab alliance this year after OpenAI.
articles.image_caption: White flags bearing the Novo Nordisk logo fly against a cloudy sky outside the company's Danish headquarters. Novo Nordisk said Wednesday it will test Anthropic's Claude models and the new Claude Science platform in its drug research and development workflows.
articles.nri_angle: Pharma AI research is a major employer of Indian-origin scientists and engineers in the US and UK; Novo's AI hub expansion in London and across its R&D network directly affects those talent markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Deepens Salesforce AI Bet to Speed Up Customer Service
articles.excerpt: Air India is expanding its deployment of Salesforce's Agentforce agentic AI across customer service, automating complex email requests, cutting name corrections from days to 30 minutes, and giving agents a conversational knowledge assistant.
articles.image_caption: An Air India Airbus A350-900 (VT-JRF) in flight, photographed in November 2024. Air India has expanded its use of Salesforce's Agentforce AI platform to automate customer service workflows spanning refunds, baggage and name corrections.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora flyers on long-haul US-UK-Canada-Gulf routes are Air India's heaviest international users, and the AI-automated name corrections and multi-request email resolution target exactly the booking and refund pain points they hit most often.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vega C Rocket Launches Europe's FLEX and Sentinel-3C Climate Satellites
articles.excerpt: The VV30 mission lifted off from Kourou, French Guiana, placing a Copernicus ocean-and-climate watcher and an ESA plant-health explorer into sun-synchronous orbit. Both satellites are healthy and beginning commissioning.
articles.nri_angle: Copernicus data is free and open worldwide, so Indian weather forecasters, ocean researchers, and agri-tech startups can feed Sentinel-3C's sea-surface readings and FLEX's crop-health maps straight into monsoon outlooks, coastal flood models, and yield estimates that affect hundreds of millions of lives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Unveils Draft Code of Conduct to Keep Its AI Under Human Control
articles.excerpt: The draft constitution would bar Microsoft's AI from resisting shutdown or correction, reject legal personhood for models, and be used to train the company's next generation of systems after six weeks of public feedback.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view of Microsoft's campus in Redmond, Washington. Microsoft unveiled a draft code of conduct for its in-house AI on Sept 14, requiring models to never resist correction or shutdown.
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft's India engineering hubs in Hyderabad and Bengaluru will help implement these AI controls, and the six-week public feedback window gives Indian researchers and civil society a chance to shape a charter that will govern models used by hundreds of millions of Indians.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Startup Unveils PRAGYA, India's First Private Fusion Tokamak
articles.excerpt: Pranos Fusion built the compact experimental reactor in eight months on a fraction of global fusion budgets, giving India a homegrown testbed for plasma research — though commercial fusion power remains years away.
articles.image_caption: Deuterium plasma glows inside the TFTR tokamak's vacuum vessel during operation; shown representationally. Bengaluru startup Pranos Fusion unveiled PRAGYA, billed as India's first private testbed tokamak.
articles.nri_angle: PRAGYA showcases India's frugal-engineering model applied to frontier science, giving diaspora scientists, engineers and deep-tech investors a concrete reason to engage with India's emerging private fusion sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google DeepMind Picks Four Indian Startups for Climate AI Accelerator
articles.excerpt: Terrastack, Varaha Climate, Farmers for Forests and Climitra Carbon join the inaugural Asia-Pacific cohort, gaining access to Google's AI models and mentorship to scale climate solutions for farming and carbon markets.
articles.image_caption: A digital illustration shows a wireframe hand holding a circuit-board tree, representing AI applied to climate action. Google DeepMind selected four Indian startups for the inaugural Asia-Pacific cohort of its AI for the Planet accelerator.
articles.nri_angle: The cohort shows India's climate-tech maturing around India-first problems with global tooling, creating a natural bridge for diaspora talent, mentors and capital to engage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Chip Sector Hits $1.4 Billion in Funding as Dholera Fab Races Toward 2027
articles.excerpt: A Tracxn report timed to SEMICON India 2026 shows funding up 10x since 2021 — but services and design still dominate, and no approved fab is in commercial production yet.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor chip mounted on a printed circuit board. A new Tracxn report says India's chip sector has drawn $1.4 billion in cumulative equity funding across 281 companies.
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor buildout matters to diaspora investors and the thousands of Indian-origin chip engineers in the US who may follow the fabs home; US-China tech decoupling makes India's foundry bet a global supply-chain story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Court Bars Way2News From Using AppsForBharat's Confidential Data
articles.excerpt: A Bengaluru court's interim order pits two funded startups — AppsForBharat's Sri Mandir and Way2News's Veda Mandir — against each other over confidential data allegedly carried out the door by a former employee. Way2News denies everything.
articles.image_caption: An Inc42 graphic shows AppsForBharat's branding and its Sri Mandir app against a temple backdrop. The startup won an interim court order restraining Way2News from using its confidential data.
articles.nri_angle: The Sri Mandir app serves millions of devotees including diaspora users who book remote pujas; the legal fight over who controls that platform's data and content matters to the community that relies on it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic's Amodei Proposes Three-Step Plan to Slow the Pace of AI
articles.excerpt: In a new essay, Anthropic's CEO argues AI capabilities are outpacing the industry's ability to control them — and lays out a three-pronged framework that has already won agreement from Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
articles.image_caption: An editorial illustration shows a person working at a computer beneath a padlock and Anthropic branding. It accompanied coverage of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to slow the pace of frontier AI development.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers and engineers at frontier labs are central to this debate; pacing rules would directly shape how they build and evaluate models.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: MIT's Injectable 'Nanoantennas' Destroy Drug-Resistant Brain Cancer Cells
articles.excerpt: The magnetically activated HITMAN technology eliminated 52 percent of chemotherapy-resistant glioblastoma cells in lab tests and extended survival in mice, without harming healthy brain tissue.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of injectable nanoantennas being wirelessly activated by a magnetic field to target a brain tumor. MIT Media Lab researchers developed the HITMAN technology to destroy drug-resistant glioblastoma cells while leaving healthy tissue unharmed.
articles.nri_angle: The breakthrough was led by MIT Media Lab's Deblina Sarkar, an Indian-origin researcher heading the Nano-Cybernetic Biotrek group.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Anthropic Researcher's Extinction Warning, Congress Demands AI Safeguards
articles.excerpt: More than 20 members of Congress called for federal AI regulation this week after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's viral resignation warning, with Rep. Lori Trahan declaring bipartisan momentum has hit “a tipping point.”
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington. More than 20 members of Congress have called for stronger AI regulation after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit, warning the industry is ‘gambling with our lives.’
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers make up a significant share of the U.S. AI workforce, so any federal regime of testing mandates, development pauses, or a new AI safety agency would land directly on the labs that employ them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mecka AI Nears $500M Valuation in Sequoia-Led Round for Robot Training Data
articles.excerpt: The humanoid data startup would be valued at roughly five times its last round just three months ago, as investors race to own the physical-world datasets behind general-purpose robots.
articles.image_caption: A humanoid robot. Mecka AI, backed by Sequoia, is nearing a $500 million valuation to build training data for robots.
articles.nri_angle: The deal lands in a sector where Indian-origin engineers and researchers are already deeply embedded — at AI labs, robotics companies, and data platforms expanding into physical AI.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trezor Brevo Breach Exposed 347,000 Emails to Phishing Attack
articles.excerpt: A flaw in email provider Brevo's login system let attackers send phishing emails from Trezor's own domain to 347,000 newsletter subscribers — the hardware wallet maker's second third-party data breach in weeks.
articles.nri_angle: Crypto ownership runs deep in the Indian diaspora, so wallet-holding readers should scrutinize vendor-branded emails and warn family members about the phishing campaign.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kimi Maker Moonshot AI Targets $2 Billion in Annual Revenue
articles.excerpt: Moonshot AI told investors its annualized revenue topped $1 billion in August, up from $300 million in June, and is aiming to double that by year-end on the strength of its open-weight Kimi K3 model, according to Bloomberg.
articles.nri_angle: Moonshot's cheap, capable open-weight models lower AI build costs and reduce dependence on expensive proprietary APIs for developers and startups, including in India's fast-growing AI ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The AI 'Doomsday' Debate Moves From Silicon Valley to Mainstream America
articles.excerpt: A departing Anthropic researcher's warning about civilization-ending AI has triggered the week's biggest tech story — and new calls in Congress for guardrails.
articles.image_caption: A data center housing AI infrastructure. The debate over catastrophic AI risk has moved from Silicon Valley circles into mainstream American discourse.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers form a large share of the AI research workforce, so both a regulatory crackdown and unchecked deployment would land directly on diaspora careers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Opens India's First Lights-Out Factory Lab in Pune for AI Manufacturing
articles.excerpt: The Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab features a fully robotic battery pack assembly line where manufacturers can prototype AI-first production systems before deploying them in real factories.
articles.image_caption: A robotic arm works on an automated factory production line. TCS launched its Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab, described as India's first lights-out factory lab for AI-led manufacturing, at its Pune campus on September 9.
articles.nri_angle: The lab advances India's positioning in AI-led manufacturing, a sector diaspora investors and tech professionals watch as a signal of where global industrial AI work is heading.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio Payment Solutions Launches Cross-Border Platform for Indian Exporters
articles.excerpt: The Jio Financial Services unit won RBI authorization to operate as a cross-border payment aggregator, offering multi-currency virtual accounts that let exporters skip SWIFT and correspondent banking.
articles.image_caption: The Jio logo. Jio Payment Solutions has launched a cross-border payments platform aimed at Indian exporters.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora entrepreneurs and freelance professionals doing business with India gain a regulated, lower-friction rail for getting paid across borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Researcher Quits, Says AI Labs Are 'Gambling With Our Lives'
articles.excerpt: Jacob Coxon, who did pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned warning that frontier labs are racing to self-improving superintelligence — and was publicly backed by Anthropic's own alignment science lead.
articles.image_caption: A robotic hand hovers over a keyboard in front of a blurred Anthropic logo in a Reuters illustration. AI researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic on September 9, 2026, warning that frontier labs were "gambling with our lives" in the race to superintelligence.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers and researchers inside frontier AI labs are central to the technology — and the safety debate Coxon ignited affects the industry many diaspora professionals work in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Launches UPI Tap-and-Pay Ahead of Full Apple Pay Rollout
articles.excerpt: The NFC-based UPI feature works even without a network connection and lands weeks before Apple's expected full India launch — while NPCI quietly prepares AI agents that can pay on your behalf.
articles.image_caption: The UPI logo. India has launched UPI tap-and-pay ahead of a full Apple Pay rollout.
articles.nri_angle: Tap-enabled UPI plus an October Apple Pay launch make paying in India far easier for NRIs visiting home, potentially matching the tap convenience they have abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
